_doc: The estate's liveness contract. Every capability declares what it must PRODUCE and how
often. A capability with no declared observable is UNPROVEN — a finding, not a pass.
Why this file exists (measured 2026-08-05):
- meta/ESTATE_PAUSED was set 2026-08-02T18:56 and the estate did nothing for 3d 4.5h
while verify_estate.sh reported 'coordinator last_tick 15s ago' and the morning brief
ran daily. Every light was green.
- 21 of 25 enabled cron jobs had no declarable output, so 'did it work' was unanswerable.
- daily-strategist-audit errored once, auto-disabled, dead 7d. otto-dispatch off 46d.
- pull_project_work skipped every project with an empty objective queue, 3d, silently.
None of those were FAILURES. They were SILENCES, and nothing in the estate detects silence.
observable kinds:
file       — newest mtime across `path` (glob ok) proves production
sqlite     — `query` must return one epoch-seconds column; newest row proves production
json_field — glob `path`, keep only records matching `where`, then take the newest.
Filters on CONTENT before freshness. Use it whenever a file being
written does not by itself mean anything happened.
receipt    — measured production from cron/scheduler.py::_write_receipt, which
records the files each job run touched. `requires: artifacts` means a
run only counts if it wrote a non-log file; `requires: exit0` is the
weaker bar, correct only for jobs whose output leaves the filesystem
(a Telegram message). Every exit0 row says so in its note.
none       — NOT DECLARED. Audits as UNPROVEN. Declare it; never delete the row.
The distinction the whole file turns on: a cron last_run_at proves a job RAN. It never
proves it DID anything. That is the signal that read green through the three-day outage,
and it is why no verdict here is allowed to derive from it.

Drift detection between declared and actual estate state
Curate the pending digest the dispatcher reads
capabilities.note: Was kind:file on queue/pending-digest.json until 2026-08-06. That file is CONSUMED by the dispatcher (otto-dispatch.py:164, os.replace -> .processed), so it is legitimately absent between a dispatch tick and the curator's next write. Two audit runs five minutes apart read PRODUCING then DARK with nothing actually wrong — a false DARK on the estate's own alert chain, delivered hourly. The curator's receipt is the honest observable: it records that the curator ran and wrote, independent of whether the consumer has since eaten the file.

capabilities.note: Last run 17:19 exited 1 with API Error: Unable to connect to API (ENOTFOUND). The 23:19 run did not fire. 2026-08-17: the real cause of DARK was not the ENOTFOUND above. observable.requires_note: reflection_pulse.py:124-131 hashes its payload and, when nothing changed since the last pulse, prints '[pulse] <ts> no-change' and returns 0 WITHOUT writing a file. Writing is conditional by design, so requires=artifacts scores a quiet estate as a dead capability: measured 2026-08-07 it read DARK at 25/53 while a manual run exited 0 and emitted pulse-20260807-074040.md on the very next state change. Same shape as improvement_probe. exit0 is the honest bar and is the WEAKER claim — it proves the pulse evaluated state, not that state moved.

capabilities.note: Reports a clean tree as a legitimate no-op. period_s corrected 3600 -> 21600 on 2026-08-17. capabilities.what: Escalation actually reaches the founder (not merely gets produced)
capabilities.note: Every other capability here measures PRODUCTION. None measured DELIVERY, which is the link that actually failed: otto-dispatch sat disabled 46 days while everything upstream produced correctly and 1,519 alerts went nowhere. The canary rides the real relay (cron tick -> no_agent stdout -> _deliver_result -> telegram) and confirms the PREVIOUS run's arrival by reading last_delivery_error off its own job record (cron/jobs.py:978), so it never trusts its own report of success. Note the circularity this cannot escape: if delivery is broken, the alarm about delivery cannot be delivered either. The non-circular check is the pull-side ALERTS section of verify_estate.sh, which reads state/delivery_proof.json by hand.

requires=ran, not exit0, and the first receipt proved why: this job exits 1 to REPORT a breach (2026-08-07: 'Claude spend $220.82 of $120 cap (1,212 requests)', WARN delivered: True). Scoring it on exit0 inverts the alarm — the sentinel would look deadest exactly when it was working hardest. Its own delivery is the real alert; this capability only asserts the sentinel is still running at all.

Registered 2026-08-07 when launchd jobs joined the receipt layer. Bar changed exit0 -> ran on 2026-08-17, measured: 162 runs in 7 days, 0 with exit code 0. The sweep was not failing. Its exit code is the ESTATE's freshness verdict, not the job's health: scripts/graphify_sweep.py:418 is 'return 0 if ok else 1' where ok = (absent==0 and stale==0 and tracked==0 and not hook_problems). A crash raises instead, so exit 1 never means the job broke. exit0 therefore scored a working job DARK whenever any repo was stale — the same false-alarm class the health_watchdog note records. Freshness stays visible elsewhere: the sweep prints its own VERDICT line and SessionStart prints the graph banner. Do NOT tighten back to exit0 until the script separates 'the sweep ran' from 'the estate is fresh'.

capabilities.what: Off-machine snapshot of the hermes-agent submodule (all agent code)
capabilities.note: Split out of cron:hermes-config-auto-push on 2026-08-07. It had run hourly inside that job's 120s cap while its push needs far longer — it pushes a PARENTLESS commit, so git cannot negotiate a delta against a shallow clone and re-uploads the whole tree every run. Result: the snapshot never completed, and it set problems=1 on every parent sync, which is the real reason config_auto_push read DARK while the parent sync worked. The parent repo's own backup is config_auto_push; this covers the submodule, which the parent stores only as a gitlink SHA.

capabilities.what: The working-method scoreboard: founder-stop rate, complaint clusters, output tokens per tool call. Read by the Ops Console /method page.
capabilities.note: The load-bearing check, because a FROZEN snapshot renders on the console page exactly like a stable one. Measuring the artifact rather than the job is what makes 'the number stopped moving' visible at all. DARK at 3x period = 12h. Paired with method_scoreboard_job, which says WHY it went dark.

capabilities.what: The scheduled run that produces the method scoreboard
capabilities.note: requires=exit0 is the WEAKER bar and is chosen deliberately. launchd_receipt._scan_produced walks the wrapper's own root; reflect.py writes outside it, into ~/Documents/code/prospector/store/ops, so every run records artifact_count 0. Under requires=artifacts this capability would read DARK forever while the job was working perfectly. The exit-0-did-nothing case that exit0 therefore cannot catch is covered by method_scoreboard, which measures the artifact itself.

capabilities.what: The agent writes what it learned to persistent memory — the whole premise of the product
capabilities.note: Measured 2026-08-17: MEMORY.md sat at 3,234/3,300 chars from 5 Aug, so every lesson longer than 66 characters was REFUSED by MemoryStore.add and dropped. Twelve days of silent non-learning with every light green. The cap is now 6,000 and this capability is what makes the next jam visible: no write in 3 days = DARK.

capabilities.what: Every agent turn is captured as ShareGPT training data
capabilities.note:
Wired 2026-08-17. The capability was in the product from the start and never switched on: save_trajectories defaulted to False and nothing in the estate passed it.

2026-08-17: proved the whole chain except real traffic. config.yaml:601 sets trajectories.enabled: true; agent/agent_init.py turns save_trajectories on from that key for the callers that never pass the flag (the gateway and the cron scheduler, which is all of the estate's real traffic) — before that the whole path was dead wiring. Sink measured directly: save_trajectory() wrote 231 bytes to ~/.hermes/trajectories/trajectory_samples.jsonl. That probe row was DELETED rather than left in place, because a synthetic write would make this capability read PRODUCING without a single real turn behind it. It stays DARK until the gateway or the scheduler runs one agent turn, which is the correct reading.

CLOSED 2026-08-17. ~/.hermes/trajectories/trajectory_samples.jsonl now holds a real row (54,793 bytes) written by AIAgent._save_trajectory on an agent built from the live config, with save_trajectories reading True off the config gate. The row came from a verification turn, not from a model call: two attempts to drive a real turn through run_agent.py both died in the provider (HTTP 404 with no model set, then 'Connection error' against https://api.minimax.io/anthropic), and a turn that fails in the API writes nothing at all — not even to failed_trajectories.jsonl, because turn_finalizer never runs. So what is proven here is the estate's whole side of the chain: config key, init gate, _convert_to_trajectory_format, sink path and file write. Only the model call is unproven, and it is not this capability's job.

capabilities.what: The engine's daily offsite copy of the store to Cloudflare R2, taken on Fly
capabilities.note: Registered 2026-08-20. The job has run daily since the engine moved to Fly and was graded by nothing: supervisord.conf wrapped four jobs in receipt.sh and scripts/engine_failover.py held a hand-written tuple of two, so the receipt was written onto the volume and never collected. The tuple is gone - the bridge now reads the keys out of supervisord.conf (container_receipt_keys). requires=exit0, not artifacts: receipt.sh writes artifact_count 0 for every job, so requiring artifacts would score this DARK on a perfect run, which is the false-alarm trap already recorded in the prospector_watchdog note.

capabilities.what: The weekly proof that a backup can actually be restored, not merely written
capabilities.note: Registered 2026-08-20, same gap as offsite_backup. This is the more expensive one to be blind about: a backup nobody has restored is a belief, not a backup, and DAT-2 in docs/LAUNCH_OPS_PROGRAM.md is open for exactly that reason. exit0 is the right bar because scripts/restore_drill.py writes store/ops/restore_drill.json on pass AND on fail and exits non-zero on fail, so a drill that ran and failed is not silently a drill that passed.

latches.what: CEO kill-switch. Blocks the ENTIRE tick before any work is admitted.
latches.note: Set 2026-08-02T18:56, still set 3d 4.5h later. No event row, no audit line, no owner, no reason recorded — set_estate_paused writes an 18-byte file and nothing else. The estate cannot tell you who paused it.
latches.release_policy: NOT auto-releasable, deliberately: a kill-switch that clears itself is not a kill-switch. It escalates every run until a human resolves it — which is exactly the behaviour that was missing for 3.2 days.

latches.what: Cron jobs switched off. A disabled job reports last_status='ok' — it looks healthy because it is not failing, it is simply not running.
latches.note: otto-dispatch off since 2026-06-20 (46d), otto-improvement-pulse since 2026-06-21, daily-strategist-audit auto-disabled 2026-07-29.
latches.release_policy: NOT auto-releasable: re-enabling a job the founder switched off deliberately would change estate behaviour without being asked, and daily-strategist-audit would simply re-fail (its script field is null). Escalates instead, so a 46-day silence surfaces on day one.

latches.what: Breakers left open. A breaker with no cooldown is a latch, not a breaker.
latches.release_policy: Auto-releasable. A breaker is supposed to have a cooldown; one that stays open until a human notices is a latch wearing a breaker's name. Re-opens immediately if the underlying fault is still there, which is the correct behaviour.

latches.what: Enabled jobs that have never run. last_run_at=None means there is NO status at all — the absence a failure-watcher cannot see.
latches.release_policy: Cannot be released — an enabled job that never fired needs diagnosis, not a switch flip. Escalates so the absence becomes a visible failure.
